text: Astronomy begins with stars, celestial bodies powered by nuclear reactions in their cores, which produce light and heat. Stars form in vast molecular clouds, their orbits determined by distance and speed, and their lives are shaped by the gravitational forces that govern their motion. Over time, stars create craters on other celestial bodies, like planets and moons, through meteorite impacts that reshape their surfaces. On Earth and the Moon, these craters can be seen, providing valuable insights into the history and evolution of the planets. Studying these celestial bodies not only reveals the intricate workings of the universe but also the dynamic processes that have shaped our own planet.
summary: Astronomy starts with stars, their orbits determined by distance and speed, forming craters from meteorite impacts, and visible on Earth or Moon.
